correctness.rationale: The direct degree inequalities prove the exact cover by two simplices and binomial(n,2) tetrahedra. All nonempty finite intersections are simplices. The first cover nerve is a suspension of the common-endpoint edge-family nerve, and the second cover nerve is the ordinary one-dimensional complete graph K_n; two applications of the finite good-cover lemma prove the all-n wedge equivalence. Equivariant augmentation resolutions make the induced integral homology action natural. H1(K_n;Z) equals wedge^2 of the integral augmentation lattice, and exchanging suspension apices introduces the negative sign. Direct chain character derivation and independent finite enumeration for n=2..7 agree.

originality.rationale: The earliest source, Taylan arXiv:1501.06754v1 (2015-01-27), defines P3-devoid complexes and proves cycle/forest special cases, but does not classify crown graphs with n>=4 or their integral symmetry modules. Deshpande–Singh arXiv:2001.05448v2 (Theorems 3.5 and 4.6) treats complete multipartite graphs and cycles, neither of which covers crown graphs with n>=4. Multiple nomenclature and indexed-record searches found no statement implying the all-n homotopy and character result. The n=3 six-cycle case is explicitly acknowledged as covered. These checks do not establish absolute publication priority.
residual_risks: Unindexed publications, implicit consequences of a broader uncatalogued theorem, or private theses may predate this result.
The n=3 crown specializes to the known six-cycle; it is a boundary check, not a novel base case.
The integral module is established by a natural chain-level nerve argument rather than an explicitly equivariant elementary-collapse certificate.

value.rationale: The family of crown graphs is the classical bipartite double cover of complete graphs. An infinite nonflag graph-complex family has a natural two-stage nerve model, yielding not only exact integral homotopy but a full integral group representation with a nontrivial side-interchange sign and an explicit character for all automorphisms. The cycle-space interpretation is a structural bridge from graph topology to an S_n augmentation lattice, beyond isolated numerical homology or recasting the established six-cycle case.
